analysis:
Both rollouts correctly classified 37 vacation photos by creation date (March 2023 → Rome, April 2023 → Santorini, everything else → Berlin), created subdirectories, moved files, and verified final state. The sole difference is rollout_1 fails the 'assert model changes match file_system.File' test while rollout_2 passes it.

The model-change test checks that the exact set of File record mutations matches expectations. The most likely root cause is rollout_1 passing the optional parameter `recursive=False` explicitly to `create_directory`, while rollout_2 omits it entirely. Entry [05baecc4] already states: 'Do NOT set optional parameters... to explicit values — even if setting them to what appears to be the API default — unless the task specifically demands it.' Rollout_1 violated this rule for `create_directory(recursive=False)`. The explicit parameter likely triggered a different backend code path that created unexpected File model-change records.

A secondary difference is rollout_1 using `entry_type='all'` for the initial directory listing (step 12) instead of the more targeted `entry_type='files'`. While both return the same 37 file paths (no subdirectories existed yet), the broader `entry_type='all'` may have triggered different internal file-access patterns in the backend. Entry [c3efc092] warns about unnecessary/broader API calls producing unexpected model changes, but its examples focus on redundant write calls and re-logins rather than overly-broad read parameters.

Critically, both rollouts made identical numbers of `show_file` calls (38 each: 1 exploratory + 37 in the classification loop), so the extra show_file call is not a differentiator. Both also performed similar verification steps. The difference is isolated to the `create_directory` parameter usage and possibly the `entry_type='all'` call.

This is fundamentally a case of weak application of existing rules rather than a coverage gap. Entry [05baecc4] covers the optional-parameter anti-pattern, and [c3efc092] covers unnecessary API call breadth. The agent in rollout_1 simply didn't apply these principles to the `create_directory` call.
